pr_title: Don't crash sensor platform on unnamed tplink devices
pr_body:
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

`assert` inside the integration code causes a crash if the device is reporting an empty name (`""`).
This PR narrows the type by checking the instance type instead of its value.
Marking this as a draft for now as it's unclear if this might bring some issues, i.e., when there are multiple sockets having such a name.

Regression from https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/108710

issue_context.body:
### The problem

To be fair I am not a 100% positive it was 2024.2, but it was released on the 7th and the last reported date of consumption was on the 8th. My HA auto updates, and not sure how to see when it updated. However, the timing seems to match up.

This has caused a bunch of my automations to fail, and I'm also now not capturing daily power usage.

Maybe the firmware got updated and it started to return something else than an empty string for the name, as I don't think there have been related changes in homeassistant. You could use the `kasa` tool in the console to verify that if you want, but we should still fix the issue with empty names.

P.S. no need to highlight names in issue comments, anyone subscribed will be informed automatically :-)

review_comments: Honestly, this would then name the device `""`, I am not sure if that's what we want. If the name can be falsey, we should take a default string to name the device (not sure if there is a recognizable name other than the alias)

Yeah, that was my concern, too. So basically what we want is something like this, but I'm unsure if it's currently doable?
```
alias = device.alias or tr("Socket")
```
Having non-recognizable names when no name is given shouldn't be an issue given they can be renamed manually. Alternatively, we could use the device id (which is done for the unique_id) if no name is available, but they look rather ugly as they are 42-char hex-encoded strings.
